clue.text: Patient support for tasteless plot

parts.note: a sick joke is a tasteless one
a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: Someone asks what support is available for a garden plot of poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickbed is where a patient lies, so it literally supports someone who is ill.

clue.text: Trumpet's first to be replaced by piano in chamber groups raised in flat landscape

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and another letter is put in its place
in a down clue, raised means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: septets are groups of seven chamber musicians

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word trumpet as the one taken

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: In chamber music groups a pianist stands in for the trumpeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SEPTETS into STETPES; 'to be replaced by' swaps its second T (Trumpet's first) for P, giving STEPPES.
explanation.definitionFit: Steppes are the vast treeless grassy plains of Eurasia, a famously flat landscape.

clue.text: Heard someone doing wrong song — "Where the Dead Men Go"

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken for its sound when spoken

parts.note: a sinner is someone doing wrong
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is heard singing a song with a grim title about the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: CINERARIA is a plural of cinerarium, a place where cremated ashes are kept. The title echoes a pop song, which hides the definition in a piece of quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineraria (plural of cinerarium) are repositories for the ashes of the cremated, so the dead go there.

clue.text: Woodworker's companion

parts.note: a worker is a bee, as in a worker bee
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A carpenter's mate or companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'Woodworker's' splits into 'Wood' (the definition) and 'worker's companion' (the wordplay); the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech is a hardwood timber, a type of wood used in furniture making.

clue.text: Broadcaster dropping by to take bearings and mislead

indicators.note: to take means one piece holds another piece inside it
dropping means the word by is removed from the name

parts.note: David Dimbleby is a veteran British TV broadcaster
SSE, south-south-east, is a compass bearing made of several points

explanation.surface: A broadcaster pops in to get his bearings and then misleads people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes a word that is printed in the clue itself, leaving the broadcaster's surname shorn of its last two letters; 'to take' then holds the compass bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to conceal one's true motives, which means to mislead others.

clue.text: Seafood that's the object of heart-warming exercise

definitions.meaning: small edible shellfish sold as seafood
the idiom says something warms the ___ of your heart

explanation.surface: A shellfish is the target of a cheerful workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition relies on the idiom 'it warms the cockles of my heart', meaning it pleases deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles are small edible bivalves, and the idiom names the depths of the heart.

clue.text: Do talk about Spain!

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to chat is to talk
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An urging to go and discuss Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for to swindle or deceive them.

clue.text: Decoration for eunuch holding a knight up

indicators.note: holding means the first piece surrounds the others

parts.note: a capon is a castrated cockerel, a eunuch among birds

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A eunuch is decorated for lifting a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the knight's title, as this is a down clue; 'holding' wraps the bird round A and that reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth covering for a horse, a kind of decoration.

clue.text: Money wrapped in note to scrubber

indicators.note: wrapped in means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash is wrapped inside a note sent to a scrubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is a fibrous sponge used for scrubbing the skin in the bath.

clue.text: With charm and cunning, taking little time

indicators.note: taking means the first piece contains the others

parts.note: sly means cunning
wee is Scots for little

explanation.surface: Someone charming and crafty takes very little time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sweetly means doing it charmingly or pleasantly.

clue.text: Boy from Northern Ireland turned outside

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second
turned means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A lad from Ulster gets turned outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Ireland' looks like one unit (NI) but splits: 'turned' gives ERIE from EIRE, and 'outside' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a boy's name, a short form of Ernest.

clue.text: Enclosure for farm animals or duck, almost Dickensian inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within the other
almost means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a scoter is a type of sea duck
Uriah Heep is a character from Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A pen for livestock or a duck nearly houses a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the duck's last letter; 'inside' places the Dickens surname after its first letter. 'Dickensian' stands for one character, Uriah Heep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepcote is a shelter or pen for sheep, which are farm animals.

clue.text: Bridge hands in training get something to write on

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside another

parts.note: PT is physical training
an arch is a bridge-like structure
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Card players in training get a notepad.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin used as a writing surface.

clue.text: Ruler keeping nothing back from cook

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in reverse
keeping means the first piece holds the second

parts.note: a tsar was the ruler of Russia
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A ruler withholds nothing from the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts O inside TSAR to make TSAOR, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in an oven.

clue.text: A less than meaty bit of science paper, pejoratively speaking

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science
rag is a scornful word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A thin piece in a science journal is dismissed scornfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag is the bony neck end of mutton, a cut with little meat.

clue.text: Regrouped after Geri's London catastrophe

indicators.note: regrouped means the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: Geri, as in the Spice Girl, given as written

explanation.surface: A pop group reforms after Geri's departure, a catastrophe for London.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Spice Girls regrouping after Geri Halliwell left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Fire of 1666 destroyed much of the City of London.

clue.text: "Drop them!" — proverbial expression in Asian city

indicators.note: in means this piece sits inside the city's name

parts.note: Bombay is the former name of Mumbai in India
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: An order to drop something becomes a proverb heard in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombs away is the call made as a bomber releases its payload, so an order to drop them.

clue.text: Skin trouble salesman gets from vegetable

parts.note: mange is a skin disease of animals
a tout is a pushy seller, as of tickets

explanation.surface: A salesman picks up a skin complaint from a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a pea with an edible pod, a vegetable.

clue.text: Dramatist receiving degree from IT officer

indicators.note: receiving means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: John Webster was a Jacobean dramatist
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A playwright receives a degree from an IT department.
explanation.definitionFit: A webmaster is the person in charge of a website, a kind of IT officer.

clue.text: Adaptable character making mess of clean home

indicators.note: making a mess of means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A versatile person makes a mess of a clean house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a lizard that changes colour, and figuratively a person who adapts readily.

clue.text: Puppet producing a lot of litter?

definitions.meaning: a person used as a tool by another
read as cats producing litter, a whimsical second sense

explanation.surface: A puppet that makes a lot of mess.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's paw is a dupe, from the fable of the monkey using a cat's paw to pull chestnuts from the fire; litter also means a brood of kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's paw is someone used as a tool by another, much like a puppet.

clue.text: Get hold of deceased VIP

parts.note: to nab is to catch or get hold of
ob is short for obiit, Latin for died

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab a dead dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a wealthy, important person, originally a returned colonial grandee.

clue.text: Conductor, oddly, became hot

indicators.note: oddly means the letters are arranged in a strange way

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A conductor strangely became hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call to take odd letters, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Beecham was a famous English orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Understood to be coming back somewhat tosticated

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read from right to left
somewhat means only some of the letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A drunk's speech is understood to be coming back, a bit befuddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosticated' is a jocular word for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken but understood or implied.

clue.text: 5 down with firm religious ethos

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A firm that cheats, but with a religious ethos.
explanation.definitionFit: To cozen is to trick or deceive, a synonym of cheat.

clue.text: Force to renew involvement with fruit

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force
to re-engage is to become involved again

explanation.surface: Being forced to get involved again with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a type of green plum, a fruit.

clue.text: Novelist and teller of tales

definitions.meaning: an informer who tells tales to the police

explanation.surface: A writer of fiction and a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: A grass is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass wrote novels, and a grass tells tales on others to the police.

clue.text: Sister admits Shed is God

indicators.note: admits means the first piece lets the second inside

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
Shed is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A nun admits that Shed is God.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A numen is a divine power or presiding deity.

clue.text: Italian recipe involving one chicken's head to be plucked

indicators.note: involving means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a pizza is a classic Italian dish
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Italian dish includes one chicken's head to be plucked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' places I and C inside the dish, and the clue's own 'to' follows; 'be' is a link, so 'plucked' alone defines a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizzicato is a musical direction meaning the strings are plucked rather than bowed.

clue.text: Prove equal to the contest

definitions.meaning: to be a ... for someone is to equal them
a game or competition between sides

explanation.surface: Proving equal to the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To match is to equal something, and a match is a sporting contest.

clue.text: Doubts this planet's seen 7

definitions.meaning: doubting means questioning whether something is so
the Seven ___ of the World are famous ancient sites

explanation.surface: Doubts that the world has seen seven.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' looks like a cross-reference, but it is the number seven.
explanation.definitionFit: To wonder is to doubt, and the Seven Wonders of the World are the famous ancient sights.

clue.text: Unconventionally packaged spirit aurally recounted by 23 down?

indicators.note: aurally means the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: rum in a can would be tinned rum, an unusual way to sell spirits

explanation.surface: Oddly packed booze is the subject of a story told by an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Drum is Günter Grass's best-known novel, so it is something he recounted.
